step.cmd: Determine if the application must be moved to Pending until an outstanding registration number is completed (e.g. a conversion or renewal application after an outstanding initial or recalculation registration number is finalized):

ul.li: If the application must be moved to Pending, go to step 2.
If the application does not need to be moved to Pending, go to step 4.

step.cmd: In NWS, move the CS WI to Pending as follows:

ul.li: Pending reason: Select Other .
Comments: Type “Unable to register application as outstanding registration number is not completed.”

Bring forward date: Select the appropriate option:
If the outstanding registration number has an unassigned WI, enter the due date of the unassigned WI. If the due date has been reached, enter today’s date + 10 business days.
If the outstanding registration number has a WI in Pending, enter the bring-forward date of the WI in Pending.
If the outstanding registration number does not have a WI in Pending and the outstanding registration number is for an application filed within the last 28 days, enter the date of application + 28 days.
If the outstanding registration number does not have a WI in Pending and the application was filed more than 28 days ago, enter the date of application + 44 days.

step.cmd: When the CS WI moves to the current workload, determine if the outstanding registration number is complete:

ul.li: If no, return to step 2.
If yes, go to step 4.

step.cmd: Determine which of the following situations applies:

ul.li: If an initial claim must be registered, go to step 5.
If a renewal application must be registered, go to step 25.
If no registration number is required (i.e. claim is BPNE 2 and the last ROE is still missing), go to step 28.

step.cmd: In SSO, verify that the correct mainframe is selected and register the claim as follows:

ul.li:
On the Claim Selection screen, do the following:
Social Insurance Number: Enter the client’s SIN.
Registration type: Select Initial .
Select Search .

Review the Name and Address screen. Note Note
For a commuter claim, complete the following fields as follows:
Ordinary place of residence different: Select Yes .
Residence postal code: Enter the workplace postal code.
Mailing address: Do the following:
First line of address: Enter the delivery address. If necessary, enter the apartment number on the first line after the delivery address.
Second line of address: Enter the city name, 2-letter state abbreviation and ZIP code. Separate the state abbreviation from the ZIP code with 2 spaces. The ZIP code may be either 5 or 9 digits. If the 9-digit format is used, use a hyphen to separate the fifth and sixth digits.
Last line of address: Type “United States.”
Postal code: Type “XXXXXX.”
Economic region - new and Economic region - old: Both fields are prefilled based on the client’s mailing address information. For a commuter claim, enter the economic region associated with the workplace postal code (if not prefilled when the residence postal code was entered).
Tax province: This field is prefilled based on the client’s mailing address information. For a commuter claim, select Commuters .
Responsible SCC: Do the following:
If the field is blank, enter the SCC shown on the WI History tab of the CS WI.
For a commuter claim, enter the SCC associated with the workplace postal code.
Tax credit: This field is prefilled based on the client’s information.
Select Next .
On the Application Form screen, select Next .

On the Registration screen, do the following:
Pay SCC: If the field is blank, enter the SCC shown on the WI History tab of the CS WI (the same one input in the Responsible SCC field).
Service unit: Type “01.”
Tentative BPC: If the field is blank, determine the BPC based on the client’s LDW and application date. If the registration number being obtained is for a subsequent claim, select the week after the previous claim’s LRW.
Claim source: Select Appli-web (virtual) .
Initial intake transaction (M149) required: Select Yes to generate the Initial Intake (M149) transaction.
Select Generate registration . Note
Select Next .
On the M149 - Initial Intake Data screen, select Update .

step.cmd: In SSO, determine if an error message is displayed for the Intake Data (M149) screen:

ul.li: If yes, go to step 7.
If no, go to step 28.

step.cmd: In SSO, review the M149 - Initial Intake Data screen to determine the error code and select it to display its description.
Based on the error code description, determine if the current claim can be terminated online or if IPOC action is required:

ul.li: If IPOC action is required, go to step 9.
If the claim can be terminated online, go to step 11.

step.cmd: Determine what IPOC action is required:

ul.li: To terminate an MPS claim, go to step 12.
To clear overlapping weeks on the Pay History (MHQ1) screen, go to step 10.

step.cmd: Determine if any of the overlapping weeks have been paid:

ul.li: If no, go to step 12.
If yes, go to step 17.

step.cmd: In SSO, correct the rejected M149 - Initial Intake Data transaction and update the BPC as follows:

ul.li: Tentative BPC: Enter the correct tentative BPC.
Terminate previous claim: Check Yes .
Select Update to transmit the information.
Go to step 28.

step.cmd: In NWS, create an IPOC Review (IPOC REV) WI as follows:

ul.li: Complexity: Select Level 1 .
Language: Select the appropriate language.

Destination — SCC: Select the SCC based on your regional IPOC:
Atlantic: 1826
Quebec: 2642
Ontario: 3056
Western Canada and Territories: 5903
End User: Select Next available user .

Issue: Select the appropriate issue:
MPS - Claim termination request.
Pay history summary adjustment.
BPC: Enter the BPC of claim that must be terminated.
Comments: Type “Claim termination to start a new claim — [error code].”

Details: Type the appropriate option:
To terminate an MPS claim, type “In order to start a new claim, please terminate the CS08 BPC [XXXX].”
To modify the Pay History (MHQ1) screen, type “In order to start a new claim, please clear PHS for weeks [XXXX] and greater.”
Obtained by: Select the appropriate method.
Obtained from: Select the appropriate source.
Source details: Enter the source details.
Select Save .

step.cmd: In NWS, move the CS WI to Pending as follows:

ul.li: Pending reason: Select Other .
Comments: Type “Request to [remove MPS claim/clear PHS] sent to IPOC.”
Bring forward date: Enter today’s date + 2 days.

step.cmd: When the CS WI moves to the current workload, determine if IPOC has completed the requested action:

ul.li: If no, repeat step 13.
If yes, go to step 15.

step.cmd: Ensure that the SIN is not open in SSO.
In FTS, select the Initial Intake (M149) transaction to update the BPC as follows:

ul.li: Tentative BPC: Enter the correct tentative BPC.
Select Update .
Go to step 28.

step.cmd: In FTS, determine if there is a revised registration number for the issue:

ul.li: If there is a registration number, go to step 18.

If there is no registration number, select the Registration Number (M025, M030, M035) transaction and assign one as follows:
Action: Select Assign .
Claim Source: Select 3 - Mail/Revised Decision .
Service Unit: Select 1 .
Decision type: Select 3 - Revised .
Select Update .

step.cmd: In FTS, select the Renewal/Revised (M106) transaction to automatically generate an Operational Centre Memo (MM06) as follows:

ul.li: Registration number: Select the revised registration number.
Memo (MPS): Check the box.
Contentious: Select 2 - No .
Complete: Select D - No .

step.cmd: When the Operational Centre Memo (MM06) transaction opens, send the information to IPOC as follows:

ul.li: BPC: Select the BPC of the claim that needs to be terminated.
Work item: Select 93 - Manual Pay System .
Work type: Select 35 - Claim Cancellation .
Remarks Line 1: Type “In order to start a new claim, please clear PHS for weeks XXXX and greater.
Remarks Line 2: Type “[your name and telephone number].”
Detection: Select 31 - Other new facts - entitlement review .
Infraction: Select A - Non-fraud - Earnings and employment .
Message: Select 97 - Internal Adjustment .
Contentious: Select 2 - No .
Complete: Select C - Yes .
Select Update .

step.cmd: Select the Registration Number (M025, M030, M035) transaction to transfer the registration number to IPOC as follows:

ul.li: Registration number: Select the appropriate registration number.
Action: Select Change registration flag .
Registration flag: Select 4 - Insurance Payment Operational Centre .
Select Update .

step.cmd: In NWS, move the CS WI to Pending as follows:

ul.li: Pending reason: Select Other .
Comments: Type “Request to clear PHS sent to IPOC.”
Bring forward date: Enter today’s date + 7 days.

step.cmd: When the CS WI moves to the current workload, determine if the overlapping weeks have been cleared from the Pay History (MHQ1) screen:

ul.li: If no, repeat step 21.
If yes, go to step 23.

step.cmd: Ensure that the SIN is not open in SSO.
In FTS, select the Initial Intake (M149) transaction to update the BPC as follows:

ul.li: Tentative BPC: Enter the correct tentative BPC.
Select Update .
Go to step 28.

step.cmd: Determine if the client submitted a renewal application to reactivate an established claim for a different BT than the one previously claimed:

ul.li: If yes, go to step 26.
If no, go to step 27.

step.cmd: Determine if there is an outstanding AI WI or a CR WI related to the conversion request:

ul.li: If no, go to step 27.
If yes, go step 28.

step.cmd: In FTS, select the Registration Number (M025, M030, M035) transaction and assign one as follows:

ul.li: Action: Select Assign .
Claim Source: Select 3 - Mail/Revised Decision .
Service Unit: Select 1 .
Decision type: Select 2 - Renewal .
Select Update .

step.cmd: In NWS, complete the CS WI.
